replacements.La cadena deductiva: cómo Euclides garan: The deductive chain: how Euclid guaranteed truth
replacements.Cada paso se apoya en el anterior. Si lo: Each step rests on the previous one. If the foundations are sound and the steps are valid, the conclusion is inevitable. Two thousand years of geometry worked exactly this way.
replacements.Euclides comenzó con cinco postulados. N: Euclid began with five postulates. He did not prove them: he declared them as the foundation. Everything else is built on them.
replacements.Entre dos puntos cualesquiera puede traz: A straight line can be drawn between any two points.
replacements.Una línea finita puede prolongarse indef: A finite straight line can be extended indefinitely.
replacements.Con centro en un punto y radio dado pued: A circle can be drawn with any point as center and any given radius.
replacements.Todos los ángulos rectos son iguales ent: All right angles are equal to one another.
replacements.Por un punto exterior a una recta solo p: Through a point outside a line, only one parallel to that line can be drawn. (Parallel postulate — the most debated in history)
replacements.definir con precisión los objetos sobre: precisely define the objects we reason about
replacements.Antes de demostrar nada, Euclides define: Before proving anything, Euclid defines his objects precisely. Without a clear definition, logic slips.
replacements.Lo que no tiene partes. Sin extensión, s: That which has no parts. No extension, no size: pure abstract position.
replacements.Longitud sin anchura: extensión en una s: Length without width: extension in a single dimension between two points.
replacements.El ángulo que resulta cuando una recta i: The angle formed when one straight line intersects another so that the two adjacent angles are equal.
replacements.razonar sobre los objetos con lógica pre: reason about objects with precise logic, without ambiguity
replacements.Proposición — conclusión forzada por la: Proposition — a conclusion forced by logic
replacements.El Teorema de Pitágoras no fue observado: The Pythagorean theorem was not observed: it was deduced. Euclid proved it in Proposition 47 of Book I using only axioms and definitions.
replacements.Teorema de Pitágoras · Proposición I.47: Pythagorean theorem · Proposition I.47 of the Elements
replacements.Por congruencia de triángulos (prop. I.4: By triangle congruence (Props. I.4 and I.41): the areas are equal
replacements.El cuadrado de la hipotenusa = suma de c: The square on the hypotenuse = the sum of the squares on the legs
replacements.Corolario — lo que sigue sin esfuerzo ad: Corollary — what follows without additional effort
replacements.Un corolario no requiere demostración pr: A corollary does not require a proof of its own: it follows directly from the previous theorem. The chain extends.
replacements.Si en un triángulo se cumple a² + b² = c: If a triangle satisfies a² + b² = c², then the angle opposite c is a right angle. There is no need to measure the angle: calculation is enough.
replacements.Usado por arquitectos e ingenieros desde: Used by architects and engineers since ancient Egypt (the 3-4-5 rule).
replacements.La distancia entre dos puntos (x₁,y₁) y: The distance between two points (x₁,y₁) and (x₂,y₂) is √[(x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²]. The Pythagorean theorem applied to coordinates.
replacements.Base de la geometría analítica, los gráf: Foundation of analytic geometry, computer graphics and machine learning (Euclidean distance between vectors).
replacements.Cada corolario puede convertirse en prem: Each corollary can become a premise for a new theorem. The chain does not end: modern geometry, topology and linear algebra are extensions of this same method.
